comparator.name: Computer Science
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 teaching and examination regulations, checked 2026-09-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted OER specifies ten compulsory 6-EC courses (60 EC) in Year 1. Year 2 has seven 6-EC compulsory courses and a 3-EC History of Science course (45 EC), followed here by a coherent 15-EC selection from the constrained menu: Academic Writing (3), Human-Computer Interaction (6) and Introduction to Computer Security (6). These are chosen options, not universal requirements. Year 3 has a genuinely open 30-EC minor/elective period, Automata and Complexity (6), Machine Learning (6), Philosophy and Ethics (3) and a 15-EC bachelor project. The zero-credit English test is excluded. The public year-two webpage repeats Algorithms I; the adopted OER specifies Algorithms II and controls this reconstruction.

alternatives.label: Computer systems, software and algorithms
alternatives.concept: Builds a UCR computing programme around programming, networks and operating systems, databases, software development, algorithms and mathematical foundations, with data and AI applications. UCR covers important subjects but has less structured hardware, security, systems project and formal research training than VU.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule preserves a substantial software and systems strand alongside algorithms, discrete mathematics, statistics and machine learning.
progression: Six four-course semesters in 2026–29, with PPD in Year 1 and at least six 300-level courses. The enriched UCR workbook confirms offerings and all formal prerequisites in earlier semesters; programming and mathematical gates precede advanced computing and AI.

alternatives.label: Mathematical computing and intelligent systems
alternatives.concept: Uses the same programming and systems foundation, then emphasizes numerical methods, linear systems, calculus, optimization, machine learning, robotics and human-centered AI. This is a data and modelling direction within computing rather than a claim to reproduce VU’s full CS systems curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: Advanced mathematics and robotics replace part of the software engineering and algorithms sequence while retaining foundational CS.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses change: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Linear Systems, Advanced Calculus and Robotics replace Consumer Product Design, Software Development, Advanced Algorithms and Ethics. The new sequence shifts 30 EC toward mathematical modelling and intelligent systems.
progression: Six four-course semesters in 2026–29, with PPD in Year 1 and at least six 300-level courses. The enriched UCR workbook confirms offerings and all formal prerequisites in earlier semesters; programming and mathematical gates precede advanced computing and AI.

candidates.label: AI, data modelling and intelligent systems

selection.assessment: A broad CS response and a 30-EC-distinct mathematical and AI direction are feasible. Bioinformatics is a permitted VU minor, but making it a third UCR 24-course comparison would require molecular life-science prerequisites and displace too much CS core; no equally coherent specialist sequence is available in the fixed three years. Cybersecurity is a constrained VU choice rather than a UCR specialization and lacks a comparable UCR security sequence.

notes.text: The VU degree requires computer organization, networks, a systems programming project, web technology, requirements engineering, operating systems, software design, automata and complexity, and a supervised 15-EC final project. Its selected constrained path also includes human-computer interaction and introductory security. UCR can build a substantial computing, mathematics and AI sequence, but does not reproduce all of these structured systems, security and final-project requirements.
